_comment: Application preferences, declared with exactly the parameter schema used by
every plugin's filters.json (see docs/design/adding_a_filter.md). The same
ParameterFormBuilder that renders the filter panel renders this dialog, so a
new preference needs no UI code at all - only an entry here and a reader.
Only put a constant here if a user could sensibly want it different. Values
that must be derived from the data (a ray epsilon, a bounding-box tolerance)
belong in the algorithm; per-invocation algorithm knobs belong in the owning
filter's filters.json; structural constants (buffer strides, UBO offsets) are

parameters.label: Field of view
parameters.help: Vertical field of view of the perspective camera, in degrees. Lower values flatten perspective, higher values exaggerate it.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.help: The projection a new 3D view starts in. **Perspective** is the usual camera; **Orthographic** has parallel rays, so size does not change with distance and parallel lines stay parallel, which is what you want to measure or compare against a drawing. Either way you can switch a view at any time with View > Orthographic Projection (5), or by turning Shift+wheel past the narrowest field of view. The two frame the same height at the point the camera orbits, so switching keeps what you were looking at. Reset Camera keeps the view's current projection.

parameters.label: Near clip ratio
parameters.help: Near clipping plane, as a fraction of the distance from the camera to the point it orbits. It sets depth precision: raise it if surfaces flicker against each other, lower it if geometry close to the camera gets cut away. To cut into an object, use the clipping plane instead (Ctrl+wheel in a 3D view).

parameters.label: Axis gizmo size
parameters.help: Edge length in pixels of the orientation gizmo drawn in the corner of the 3D view.

parameters.label: Reference grid on new views
parameters.help: The grid a new 3D view starts with: **None**, or a plane through the origin ruled in powers of ten with the world axes in red (X), green (Y) and blue (Z). **XY** is the floor of a scene that stands on Z, **XZ** of one that stands on Y. A view can be switched from View Settings at any time; File > New puts it back to this. An orthographic view looking straight down an axis shows the plane across its line of sight whatever this says.

parameters.label: Grid: fine lines
parameters.help: How strongly the finest of the three decades of grid lines is drawn: 0 is invisible, 1 a full-strength line, and more makes the lines brighter still (they saturate at fully opaque). It fades out by itself as it gets too dense to read.

parameters.label: Grid: middle lines
parameters.help: How strongly the middle decade of grid lines is drawn: 0 is invisible, 1 a full-strength line, more brighter. It is always shown; the other two fade in and out around it as you zoom.

parameters.label: Grid: coarse lines
parameters.help: How strongly the coarsest decade of grid lines is drawn: 0 is invisible, 1 a full-strength line, more brighter. It fades in as the view zooms out far enough for it to be readable.

parameters.label: Grid: axis line width
parameters.help: Width, in pixels, of the coloured lines that mark the world axes in the grid.

parameters.label: Grid: reach
parameters.help: How far the grid extends before it fades out, as a multiple of the default. Raise it for a scene seen from a long way off, or to see more of the floor towards the horizon; lower it to keep the grid close to what you are looking at.

parameters.label: Grid: line color
parameters.help: Color of the grid lines. The axes have their own colors, below.

parameters.label: Grid: X axis color
parameters.help: Color of the X axis in the grid.

parameters.label: Grid: Y axis color
parameters.help: Color of the Y axis in the grid.

parameters.label: Grid: Z axis color
parameters.help: Color of the Z axis in the grid.

parameters.label: Reframe camera when a mesh is added
parameters.help:
Whether opening a mesh, or a filter creating a layer, moves the camera to frame the scene.

**When the new mesh is off-screen** keeps the camera where you put it and reframes only when the addition would land outside the current view, so what arrives is always visible without a camera you set being thrown away.

**Always** reframes on every addition. **Never** leaves the camera alone; use View > Reset Camera to reframe by hand.

The first mesh into an empty document always frames the scene, whatever this is set to -- otherwise the view would open pointed at nothing.

enumOptions.label: When the new mesh is off-screen

parameters.label: History preview
parameters.help:
Where the Action History shows a state while you hover its thumbnail or one of its dots.

**In the view** draws the state's snapshot over the 3D view, inside a cloudy frame and under a *Preview* label, so it cannot be mistaken for the document itself. Nothing changes: moving the mouse away brings the live view back.

**In a popup** shows the snapshot in a floating window beside the panel and leaves the view alone.

parameters.label: Show layers while a project loads
parameters.help: Draw the view as each layer of a project arrives, so you watch the scene fill in. Turn this off to draw nothing until the whole project is in, which loads a little faster -- about a tenth on a project of forty large meshes -- because the view is not redrawn with every added layer.

parameters.label: Show debug options in the view settings
parameters.help: The current-layer outline has tuning controls that exist for developing it rather than for using it: its width, the dilate and erode radii of its mask, and a debug view that shows the intermediate masks. They keep their values whether or not they are shown. Turn this on to get them back in the View Settings panel.

parameters.label: Collapse layers when there are more than
parameters.help: How many layers the Layers panel lists expanded. A document with more layers than this shows them collapsed to one line each, which is how a project of dozens of meshes stays readable and quick to build; a document with fewer opens expanded, with each layer's counts and attributes beneath it. Layers you have expanded or collapsed yourself keep their state. The panel's Expand all and Collapse all buttons change every layer at once.

parameters.label: Drag threshold
parameters.help: How far the pointer must move, in pixels, before a press becomes a drag rather than a click.

parameters.label: Wireframe on load up to
parameters.help: Newly loaded meshes show their wireframe when they have fewer faces than this. Above it the wireframe is off, since it degenerates into a grey smear and costs draw time. Faces.

parameters.label: Flat shading up to
parameters.help: Newly loaded meshes use flat shading when they have fewer faces than this, so the tessellation stays visible; above it they use smooth shading. Independent of the wireframe threshold. Faces.

parameters.label: Selected edge width
parameters.help: Width, in pixels, of selected edges in the 3D view. It starts at the width an edge layer is first drawn with, so a selection on a polyline covers the edges it marks.

parameters.label: Point size
parameters.help: Size, in pixels, of the points of a newly loaded layer. A layer's own setting, in View Settings, changes it for that layer afterwards.

parameters.label: Edge width
parameters.help: Width, in pixels, of the explicit edges of a newly loaded layer that also has faces. A layer made only of edges takes the next preference instead.

parameters.label: Edge-only layer width
parameters.help: Width, in pixels, of the edges of a newly loaded layer that has edges and nothing else (a polyline). It is wider than the others because a polyline is all there is to see of it.

parameters.label: Wireframe width
parameters.help: Width, in pixels, of the wireframe of a newly loaded layer.

parameters.label: Default color map
parameters.help: Color map selected when a scalar field is first displayed.

parameters.label: Histogram bins
parameters.help: Number of bins in the scalar histogram overlay.

parameters.label: Log timestamps
parameters.help: Whether each log line is prefixed with a time. Elapsed counts from application start, which makes the gap between two lines easy to read directly; time of day is the wall clock. Format is hh:mm:ss.mmm.

parameters.label: Log verbosity
parameters.help: How much of the log panel is shown. Quieter entries are still recorded, so raising this reveals detail from operations that already ran. Debug adds timings, counters and internal bookkeeping.

parameters.label: Recent files
parameters.help: How many entries the recent-meshes menu keeps.

parameters.label: Merge duplicate vertices of STL files
parameters.help: STL stores every triangle with its own three corners, so a mesh read from it shares no vertices: each triangle is detached from its neighbors, and anything that needs connectivity (smoothing, closing holes, selecting connected components, remeshing) sees a heap of loose triangles. With this on, vertices at exactly the same position are merged as an STL file is opened or reloaded, as Remove Duplicate Vertices does, and triangles the merge leaves degenerate are removed. Turn it off to get the file exactly as stored. The TrueForm STL reader merges while reading, whatever this is set to.

parameters.label: Undo memory limit
parameters.help: Maximum tracked memory retained by undo history, in MiB. When crossed, alternate branches and then the oldest checkpoints are discarded down to a lower watermark. A value of 0 disables automatic byte-budget pruning.

parameters.label: Run parameterless filters immediately
parameters.help: When a filter picked from the layer context menu has nothing to ask -- Duplicate Current Layer, Remove Hidden Mesh Layers -- run it there and then instead of opening the filter panel on an empty form. Turn this off to always open the panel, which is useful when you want to read a filter's description before running it.

parameters.label: Purge undo under memory pressure
parameters.help: Allow the operating system's memory-pressure signal to prune undo history. Warning pressure uses the configured undo budget; critical pressure may clear all history. Purging is deferred until the active operation finishes.

parameters.label: Measure GPU frame time
parameters.help: Time each frame on the GPU as well, and show it in the status bar next to the CPU time. Off, the status bar says *GPU: not measured*. Measuring asks the graphics driver for timestamps on every frame, which costs a little, and takes effect the next time MeshLab starts. Setting the `QSG_RHI_PROFILE` environment variable turns it on as well.

parameters.label: Ray-tracing progress chunks
parameters.help: How many chunks the face array is split into when ray-tracing filters report progress. Higher values update the progress bar and respond to Cancel more often, at a small synchronisation cost.
